rationale: Compact profile: only the edge-case lens ran (blind and verification-gap not dispatched, acceptance skipped with no spec, standards not expected), so confidence is low and decision_needed was unavailable. Five blocking [1m]-handling defects survive: the double-suffix, statusline and version-first findings have unconfirmed reachability (whether the catalog carries literal [1m] ids, whether Claude Code reports [1m] in model.id), so they are capped at major; the misleading warning was confirmed. 0 deferred, 0 dismissed.

findings.title: Version-first 1M row rejects two-digit minors
findings.problem: The version-first row of ONE_MILLION_CONTEXT_TABLE matches `4[-_.][6-9]` followed by a separator, so an id like `claude-4-10-sonnet` fails it. The family-first 4.6+ row accepts `[1-9]\d`. That id then falls through to the default `false`.
findings.impact: A 1M-capable version-first id is judged not capable: a configured `[1m]` gets stripped to the bare id and the picker offers no 1M row. Reachability is unconfirmed because no such id is known in the live catalog today.
findings.recommendation: Align the row with the family-first rows, e.g. `/claude[-_.]?(?:[5-9]|[1-9]\d|4[-_.](?:[6-9]|[1-9]\d))(?!\d)[-_.](?:sonnet|opus|fable)/i`, and add a table test for a two-digit minor.

findings.title: Picker double-suffixes literal [1m] catalog ids
findings.problem: buildModelPickerOptions appends `[1m]` to any 1M-capable non-router rankedModel.id without checking whether the id already ends in `[1m]`. The existing test suite already models a catalog entry with deployment_name `claude-sonnet-5[1m]`, and supportsOneMillionContext returns true for it, so the picker would add `claude-sonnet-5[1m][1m]`.
findings.impact: The /model picker shows a row Claude Code cannot resolve, and choosing it breaks the session's model. Reachability is unconfirmed because it depends on whether the backend catalog exposes suffixed ids.
findings.recommendation: Skip the synthesis when the id is already suffixed: add `!ONE_MILLION_SUFFIX_PATTERN.test(rankedModel.id)` to the condition at line 376.

findings.title: Healing appends [1m] to already-suffixed replacement
findings.problem: When a retired `[1m]` model is replaced, keepOneMillion checks only the router gate and supportsOneMillionContext(ranked[0].id). It never checks whether ranked[0].id already ends in `[1m]`, so `${ranked[0].id}[1m]` can become `x[1m][1m]`.
findings.impact: The invalid id is written to CODEMIE_MODEL and the ANTHROPIC_* env vars by claude.plugin.ts, so the launch uses a model id the backend cannot resolve (broken runtime path). Reachability is unconfirmed because it depends on the catalog carrying a literal `[1m]` id.
findings.recommendation: Add `!ONE_MILLION_SUFFIX_PATTERN.test(ranked[0].id)` to keepOneMillion (or strip then re-append), and add a test with a suffixed replacement in the catalog.

findings.title: Misleading warning when [1m] is stripped
findings.problem: resolveClaudeModel (claude.models.ts:493-496) returns the bare id when a configured `<id>[1m]` is live but not 1M-capable. The plugin warning at line 405 fires on any previousModel !== selectedModel and says the model "is not available in this CodeMie catalog", followed by a `codemie models list` hint.
findings.impact: On the model tier, a user whose model is live is told on stderr that it is unavailable, which hides the real reason: the 1M context opt-in was dropped. This path was confirmed reachable and is exercised by the new test at line 160.
findings.recommendation: Return a distinguishing signal from resolveClaudeModel (e.g. a `reason` field on ClaudeModelResolution, or compare the bare ids in the plugin) and print a dedicated message such as "<id> does not support 1M context — using <bare id>".

findings.title: Routed-to widget misses [1m] router ids
findings.problem: This change always preserves a `[1m]` suffix on a live router id (claude.models.ts:489-492). isRoutingConfigured compares the statusline's reported model.id verbatim against the bare router ids from listRouterModelIds. `<router>[1m]` is therefore never matched, and the labels[modelId] lookup at line 792 misses the same way.
findings.impact: For a router session kept with `[1m]`, the statusline's routed-to widget never fires, so the user loses visibility into which backend model answered. Reachability is unconfirmed because it depends on Claude Code reporting the `[1m]` suffix in the statusline model.id.
findings.recommendation: Normalize before lookup: `parseRouterModelIds(env).has(modelId.replace(/\[1m\]$/i, ''))`, and apply the same strip to the nominal label lookup.
